subtitulo: Comida owns the afternoon; cena is light and late
introPt: A traveller walks into an empty comedor at six in the evening and asks when it actually fills up.
cenario: An empty restaurant at six becomes a lesson in Mexico's own meal clock.

dialogo.pt: Good afternoon. Come in, we have a table.

dialogo.es: ¿A qué hora sirven la comida aquí?
dialogo.pt: What time do you serve la comida here?

dialogo.es: De una a tres, más o menos.
dialogo.pt: From one to three, more or less.

dialogo.es: Para la cena, algo ligero está bien.
dialogo.pt: For dinner, something light is fine.

perguntas.pergunta: What time does la comida, the main meal, typically run?
perguntas.explica: Comida is the anchor meal, typically early-to-mid afternoon.

perguntas.pergunta: Why is the comedor empty at six in the evening?
opcoes: The main local meal already happened hours earlier
Six is too early to be open
perguntas.explica: Six falls well after comida and before the lighter cena crowd.

perguntas.pergunta: How does cena typically compare to comida?
perguntas.explica: Cena runs later in the evening and is often a lighter meal.

perguntas.pergunta: What should a traveller do to eat in the fuller, livelier room?
opcoes: Ask when comida runs and come at that time
perguntas.explica: Asking the local hour, then matching it, gets you the room the city actually eats in.

perguntas.pergunta: Where does the comida/cena rhythm not reliably apply?
perguntas.explica: Tourist-facing venues often run closer to a continuous schedule.
